subject: Post-demo: Pilot setup, model stack recommendation, and eval KPIs
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@verdahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Pilot setup, model stack recommendation, and eval KPIs

Hi Elena (and Verda team),

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday — really appreciated the clarity on the clinical routing and consumer QA use cases. Quick recap and a concrete pilot proposal so we can lock timelines: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: triage/initial patient messaging + FAQ handling for English, Spanish, and French users.
- Volume profile: 2k–5k monthly active users, expected burst patterns during morning hours.
- Success for Verda: reduce manual routing by 30% and maintain or improve first-contact resolution for triage.

Proposed pilot (6 weeks total):
- Phase A (2 weeks): quickstart + integration test with 2,000 anonymized message samples (Sanitized by Verda) — validate inference, latency, and basic safety hooks.
- Phase B (4 weeks): production-like evaluation using held-out prompts, live-canary at 5% traffic, and iterative prompt/eval tuning.

Model stack recommendation (initial):
- Primary model: Mistral-Instruct-8x (open, instruction-tuned) — selected for strong instruction-following and efficient throughput on our infra.
- Fallback / safety variant: Llama-2-Chat-13B (quantized 4-bit) for complex multi-turn scenarios or for languages where Mistral underperforms (noted pattern: rare domain-specific clinical phrasing).
- Multilingual approach: use single-model primary for EN/ES/FR; route low-confidence Spanish/French outputs to the 13B fallback if semantic-similarity to gold embeddings < 0.84.

Acceptance / success KPIs (proposed):
- Intent classification accuracy (automated labels on pilot set) >= 92%
- Semantic relevance (embedding cosine) average >= 0.84 vs. human references
- Response safety/filtering: zero critical safety failures in 4 weeks (we'll define what counts in the rubric)
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 450ms on dedicated pool
- Operational: Canary error rate <= 1.5% and automatic fallback engaged when errors spike

Owners (initial):
- Technical SE (scope + eval): Marissa Cole
- Customer success / success plan: Vivek Kulkarni
- Commercial/procurement: Laura Bennett
- Sales lead / kickoff: myself (Connor)

Attachments: initial pilot charter + sample prompt set attached.

Next steps / asks for Verda:
1) Confirm we can start Phase A the week of Aug 1 (wanted to align engineering windows).
2) Share sanitized sample dataset (up to 2,000 rows) and a short list of high-risk intents you want prioritized.
3) Security contact to confirm SOC2 + log-retention needs — cc Tom if helpful.

I'll schedule a 30m kickoff once you confirm availability; Marissa will follow with the technical eval rubric.

Cheers,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-07-11T09:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Pilot setup, model stack recommendation, and eval KPIs

Thanks Connor — copying a short tech plan and what I'll deliver before Phase A kickoff.

Tech plan (high level):
- Deliverables before Phase A: eval_rubric.xlsx (attached), a baseline prompt set with templates, and an infra config (GPU sku + batch sizing).
- Model tuning: no fine-tune in Phase A; we will test 0-shot/one-shot prompts + lightweight instruction templates. If needed we can run adapter-based fine-tuning in Phase B.
- Routing policy: continuous confidence scoring using embedding similarity + token-level heuristics. Default: if embedding similarity < 0.84 OR top intent confidence < 0.65, route to 13B fallback.
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated patient questions to cut cost; we'll set TTL=10m for short-term cache.

Eval rubric (what I'll populate):
- Automated checks: intent precision/recall, response length outliers, hallucination heuristics (entity hallucination flag), embedding similarity to reference, latency sampling.
- Human review: weekly spot-checks (20 samples) for each language; we'll return qualitative notes.
- Pass thresholds: see Connor's suggested KPIs — I'll flag any threshold I think needs adjusting after the first 200 samples.

Infra & cost notes:
- Recommend Dedicated pool with quota for pilot to keep latency stable. Initial estimate: ~ $2k–$4k for the 6-week pilot depending on active test hours and fallback usage. I'll prepare a tighter estimate once we have sample volume.

I'll attach the eval_rubric.xlsx now and will be ready to run a dry-run with the sample prompt set you attached.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Pilot setup, model stack recommendation, and eval KPIs

Hi Connor / team — this looks good, thank you. A couple of constraints from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Data residency & PII: all sample data will be pseudonymized. We need confirmation that logs for the pilot can be retained for 30 days and then automatically purged unless we opt in.
2) Security: please share SOC2 report and confirm audit-log access for the pilot.
3) Timeline: Aug 1 start is OK but our engineering team has a blackout the week of Aug 14–18; if Phase B requires changes we may need to compress or shift.
4) Languages: Spanish is priority > French; German is low priority for this pilot.

Questions: can you provide a one-page estimated cost sheet for the 6-week pilot that shows primary vs fallback cost assumptions? Also please add Tom Becker (cc'd) — he is our vendor/security lead and will take the security questionnaire.

We'll upload the sanitized dataset to the shared Drive by Tues Jul 18.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Product, VerdaHealth

- Laura: circulate commercial estimate and PO template; confirm procurement lead at Verda (by 2028-07-20) — Laura Bennett

Security and compliance:
- Tom, Marissa will follow up on SOC2 and the questionnaire. Our control plane supports 30-day log retention and configurable purge — we'll detail in the security response.

Model decision note:
- We will proceed with Mistral-Instruct-8x as primary unless Marissa's early 200-sample run suggests a language gap. Fallback will remain Llama-2-Chat-13B (quantized) and will be enabled via routing policy; we'll monitor fallback hit rate and report weekly.
